subject: Post-call recap: HelixPay cost anchors, latency goals & pilot next steps
messages:
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Nathan Riley <nathan.riley@helixpay.com>, Alyssa Chen <alyssa.chen@helixpay.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 05 Jul 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap: HelixPay cost anchors, latency goals & pilot next steps

Hi Nathan / Alyssa —

Thanks for the time today. Quick recap from our discovery so we’re aligned before we put the pilot docs together. Feel free to correct anything I’ve captured below.

Pain points you described:
- High per-decision inference cost on fraud scoring at peak traffic (even with model caching in-house).
- p95 latency spikes during morning batch windows — impacts real-time authing.
- Budget cap for inference tooling this year (~$15k/month target for production inference).

Goals we heard:
- Reduce inference unit cost by ~40% vs your current baseline, while keeping p95 under 200ms for the auth path.
- Roll out a two-stage pilot: baseline measurement (1 week) + optimizations (2–3 weeks) to validate batching / caching levers.
- Maintain SOC2 controls (security contacts below).

Levers we discussed (initial suggestions):
- Continuous batching on write-heavy endpoints (auth) to improve tokens/sec while preserving p95 with burst policies.
- Prefix/KV caching for repeated context (reducing decoder steps on low-variance prompts).
- Quantized lighter-weight model variant for initial fast pass + full model for high-confidence scoring.
- Dynamic routing: cheaper model for low-risk flows, fallback to higher-quality model for ambiguous cases.

Proposed pilot scope (high level):
- Duration: 3 weeks (1 week baseline + 2 weeks tuning), target 1M decisions/month equivalent load for measurement.
- Two endpoints: real-time auth (latency-sensitive) and batch chargeback scoring (throughput focus).
- Deliverables: baseline cost/TCO, latency profile, recommended batching/cache config, and expected unit economics path to production.

Next steps I propose:
1) I’ll circulate a one-page pilot scope + SOW template (attached) for your legal/procurement.
2) Technical deep-dive with our infra engineer and your platform/security contact — can you share the name(s)?
3) We’ll run a short cost-sensitivity table showing 3 scenarios (no levers, caching + batching, caching + batching + quantization).

Attachments: helixpay-macro-pilot-scope.pdf (stub)

If that aligns, what’s your preferred time for a technical call next week? I can do Wed/Thu mornings PT.

Thanks again — excited to help make inference predictable for HelixPay.

—
Olga Petrov
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
olga.petrov@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0142
From: Nathan Riley <nathan.riley@helixpay.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alyssa Chen <alyssa.chen@helixpay.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 06 Jul 2027 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: HelixPay cost anchors, latency goals & pilot next steps

Thanks Olga — good summary. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) Budget: we are targeting ~$15k/month for inference, but there is flexibility for a time-limited pilot if we can show clear ROI.
2) Workloads: the auth flow is ~65% of decision volume and needs strict p95 SLAs; chargeback scoring is batch-driven and tolerates higher latency.
3) Security: SOC2 and restricted IP flows are a must. Please include a security/controls call — our lead is Alyssa Chen (cc’d).

Two asks before we lock a date: 
- Can you share a simple TCO template (tokens, model cost, infra delta) so I can brief finance?
- Any initial thoughts on what kind of throughput we should provision for a 1M decisions/month pilot (just rough numbers)?

I’ve attached our SOW template (SOW_template.docx) for your legal team to review. If we can get a one-page cost comparison and a proposed week-by-week pilot schedule, we can share internally and aim to confirm the pilot by Friday.

—
Nathan Riley
Head of Platform Engineering | HelixPay
Nathan.Riley@helixpay.com | +1 (617) 555-2299
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Nathan Riley <nathan.riley@helixpay.com>
Date: Tue, 06 Jul 2027 12:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: HelixPay cost anchors, latency goals & pilot next steps

Olga — thanks for the write-up. A couple operational notes from our side: 

- We can offer a pilot credit structure that helps compress the commercial ask while we prove the savings. Propose: 50% credit on platform usage during the pilot, then a scaled reserved commitment if HelixPay hits the agreed-upon econ targets.
- I’ll own the commercial package; Marissa, can you prep a one-page cost-sensitivity that shows the three scenarios (baseline / caching+batching / caching+batching+quant) with rough token math?

Nathan — quick reply inline to your asks: 
> Can you share a simple TCO template (tokens, model cost, infra delta) so I can brief finance?

Yes — Marissa will produce that and we’ll include sample throughput numbers for 1M decisions/month (expectation: ~300–600 concurrent inference threads depending on batching aggressiveness; we’ll show headroom).

> Any initial thoughts on what kind of throughput we should provision for a 1M decisions/month pilot (just rough numbers)?

We’ll size a baseline and an optimized scenario. Baseline conservative estimate: ~450 concurrent workers (limited batching) to hit latency SLAs; optimized with batching + caching you could drop infra concurrency by ~40–60% depending on average sequence length.

I’ll coordinate the SOW template and commercial terms with Olga. Let's target a technical deep-dive Wed 07/07 10:00–11:00 PT — Olga, can you propose that in your reply?

—
Ben Carter
Director, Sales | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai

Perfect — thanks all. Wed 07/07 10:00–11:00 PT works for us; I’ve penciled it in and will send a calendar invite with a Teams link.

Immediate next items I’ll share before the call: 
- One-page pilot scope + SOW (pilot-scope-helixpay.pdf attached).
- Cost-sensitivity table (baseline / caching+batching / caching+batching+quant) — quick view in the Drive link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aB2cHelixPilotStub

Nathan — can you confirm the legal/procurement contact who will review the SOW (name + email)? Once we have that I’ll drop the SOW into DocuSign and loop in Ben for commercial terms.

Thanks — speak Wednesday.
